title: Generalization stability of the section component locus in a flat geometrically reduced family
statement: Let $g:P\to T$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with geometrically reduced fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and let $\sigma:T\to P$ be a section [def-pc-scheme]. Put $C=\{p\in P\mid p$ lies in the connected component [def-weil-connected-scheme] of $\sigma(g(p))$ in the fibre $g^{-1}(\{g(p)\})$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]$\}$. If $p$ specializes to $q$ and $q\in C$, then $p\in C$; equivalently, $C$ is stable under generalization.

source.place: Tag 055Q, lemma-connected-along-section-open-neighbourhood: generic-point and specialization argument for the relative section component

proof.text: Fix $p\leadsto q$ with $q\in C$. Choose an affine open $V\subset T$ containing $g(q)$. Continuity implies $g(p)\in V$. Replace the family by $P_V\to V$ and restrict the section. Finite presentation is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], flatness by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. The fibre $P_{g(q)}$ is geometrically reduced; taking for $k'$ an algebraic closure of $\kappa(g(q))$ in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], the geometric fibre of $g$ over $g(q)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is reduced, hence by [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change] so is the geometric fibre of $P_V\to V$ over $g(q)$. The cartesian component identity [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] identifies its locus with $C\cap P_V$. Thus proving the assertion for this restriction proves it for the given pair. Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Tag 055Q, lemma-connected-along-section-open-neighbourhood, first paragraph: affine restriction; Tag 055M

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine] to express $V$ as the inverse limit of the affine schemes $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, where $A_i$ runs over the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $A$. Use clause (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to descend $P_V\to V$ to a finitely presented $g_i:P_i\to V_i$. Use clause (2), with domain the identity $V_i\to V_i$ and codomain $P_i$, to descend the section to a map $\sigma_j:V_j\to P_j$ at a later stage. Its composite with $g_j$ becomes the identity after base change to $V$; clause (3), applied to these two maps $V_j\to V_j$, makes that equality hold at a further stage. Hence the model has an actual section, and the comparison square, including the sections, is cartesian. All stage schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated: the bases are affine, and the sources are finitely presented over them, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The stages are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], first for $V_i$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, then for $P_i$ over $V_i$.

source.place: Tag 055Q, first paragraph, descent with section using limits.tex Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation] to the model morphism $g_i:P_i\to V_i$ and the cofinal system of later affine stages; the limit morphism is the flat $P_V\to V$. Its hypotheses hold because $V_i,P_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $g_i$ is locally of finite presentation. After advancing the stage, $g_i$ is flat. The section and comparison remain valid under base change, and finite presentation persists by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Let $\rho:P_V\to P_i$, $p_i=\rho(p)$ and $q_i=\rho(q)$, and set $v_i=g_i(q_i)$. By [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change], applied to $g_i$ and $V\to V_i$, the geometric fibre $(P_i)_{\bar v_i}$ is reduced, since the geometric fibre of $P_V\to V$ over $g(q)$ is reduced (step 1). We assert nothing about other model fibres. By [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian], $q_i$ belongs to the model section-component locus $C_i$, and $\rho^{-1}C_i=C\cap P_V$. Continuity gives $p_i\leadsto q_i$. If $p_i=q_i$ the desired membership follows immediately. Otherwise the remaining steps prove $p_i\in C_i$, using reducedness of the geometric fibre only at $v_i$.

source.place: Tag 055Q, first paragraph: limits.tex Tag 04AI (lemma-descend-flat-finite-presentation), and descent of geometric reducedness at the distinguished fibre

proof.text: The source $P_i$ is Noetherian. For $p_i\ne q_i$, [lem-sbc-noetherian-specialization-trait] supplies a discrete valuation ring $R$ and $a:S=\operatorname{Spec}R\to P_i$ mapping the generic point $\eta$ to $p_i$ and the closed point $s$ to $q_i$. Form $X=P_i\times_{V_i}S$ over the composite $b=g_i\circ a$, with structure map $f:X\to S$ and projection $r:X\to P_i$. It is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. By [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change] applied to $g_i$ and $b$, the geometric fibre $X_{\bar s}$ is reduced, because $b(s)=v_i$. The closed fibre $X_s$ is then reduced. Put $k=\kappa(s)$, $\bar k$ its chosen algebraic closure, so $X_{\bar s}=X_s\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X_s$, its inverse image in $X_{\bar s}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_k\bar k)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]; as an open subscheme of a reduced scheme it is reduced, so $B\otimes_k\bar k$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] (with $N=B$), $B\to B\otimes_k\bar k$ is injective, so $B$ is reduced. Every local ring of $X_s$ is a local ring of such an affine open, so $X_s$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], again by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff].

source.place: Tag 055Q, second paragraph: properties.tex Tag 054F (lemma-locally-Noetherian-specialization-dvr) and base change to the trait

proof.text: The base change of $\sigma_i$ is a section $\sigma_R:S\to X$. The pair $(a,\operatorname{id}_S)$ defines a second section $\tau:S\to X$ with $r\circ\tau=a$; these equalities follow from the two pullback projections. Put $F=f^{-1}(\{s\})$ and let $D$ be its connected component through $\sigma_R(s)$. By [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian], applied to $r$, the membership $q_i\in C_i$ gives $\tau(s)\in D$. The scheme fibre and $F$ have the same topology by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. The discrete valuation ring is Noetherian by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; thus $S$ is a Noetherian scheme. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $f$ and to its closed fibre over the residue field shows that $X$ and $X_s$ are Noetherian. Their topologies are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] (complement reverses inclusion of closed and open sets).

source.place: Tag 055Q, second and third paragraphs: the two sections and the Noetherian closed fibre

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open], $D$ is open in $F$, and every other connected component of $F$ is open. Their union is $F\setminus D$, so $D$ is also closed in $F$. The set $F$ is closed in $X$, being the inverse image of the closed point of $S$. Consequently $F\setminus D$ is closed in $X$. Put $U=X\setminus(F\setminus D)$, an open subscheme. Its closed fibre has underlying space exactly $D$, and both closed section points lie in $U$. The topology of $U$ is Noetherian: a chain of its open subsets is a chain of open subsets of $X$, hence stabilizes. Choose the connected component $W$ of $\sigma_R(s)$ in $U$. Again [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open] makes $W$ open in $U$, hence in $X$. Since $D$ is connected and contains $\sigma_R(s)$, maximality of the connected component gives $D\subseteq W$; in particular $\tau(s)\in W$.

source.place: Tag 055Q, last paragraph: remove the other closed-fibre components, then retain the connected total-space component

proof.text: Both sections factor through the open subscheme $W$: the inverse image of $W$ under either section is open in $S$ and contains $s$, so equals $S$, since every point of the spectrum of a local ring specializes to its closed point. The factor morphisms are obtained by restricting the section maps and their sheaf maps to this open subscheme, as in [def-weil-open-immersion]. The restriction $h:W\to S$ is flat because its local-ring maps are exactly those of $f$, using [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Its closed fibre is the open subscheme $W_s\subset X_s$; each of its local rings is a local ring of the reduced $X_s$, so it is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The scheme $W$ is connected and nonempty by construction. All hypotheses of [lem-sbc-connected-generic-fibre-trait] now hold, so the generic fibre $W_\eta$ is connected and nonempty. No assertion that an arbitrary closed-subset image gives a scheme-theoretic factorization is used; both factorizations here are through an open subscheme.

The image of the connected $W_\eta$ in the topological fibre $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ is connected and contains both $\sigma_R(\eta)$ and $\tau(\eta)$; the factor sections give these two points in $W_\eta$, and [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies the scheme and topological fibres. Explicitly, a separation of this image into two nonempty relatively open and closed sets would pull back to a separation of $W_\eta$, which is impossible. Maximality of the component through $\sigma_R(\eta)$ therefore puts $\tau(\eta)$ in the relative section component of $X/S$. The cartesian identity [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] maps this membership to $p_i=r(\tau(\eta))\in C_i$. The equality $\rho^{-1}C_i=C\cap P_V$ from step 3 gives $p\in C$. This proves the stated stability under generalization, including the equality case already handled in step 3.
